findings.statement: The authored command surface is 35 markdown command files, not 46; the raw 46 count includes 11 non-command asset/contract/README files under assets/ and scripts/.

Every mirror count difference is policy-driven: CANONICAL_MIRROR_EXCLUDES={goal-opencode.md,vision.md} makes 35-2=33, and RUNTIME_NATIVE_COMMANDS re-adds two native entries for .cursor/commands and .pi/prompts, making 35.
Matrix: Claude 33 symlinks, Codex 33 copies, Cursor 33 symlinks + 2 native files, Pi 35 copies, Hermes 33 copies, Devin 0 with no commands or prompts directory.
find -type f reports .claude/commands as 0 entries because all 33 mirrored commands are symlinks; census method must count symlinks explicitly.
vision.md is three distinct files (three md5 hashes) across .opencode, .cursor and .pi; it is per-host native by construction, not a mirrored artifact.

Devin's zero-command surface is a documented operator decision whose replacement affordance is native skill discovery (/sk-doc, /sk-git); the retired mirror previously held 36 commands and failed silently under strict YAML.

Five mirrors are generator-produced and every generator implements --check, but sync-prompts-hermes.cjs --check and sync-prompts-pi.cjs --check are invoked by neither the pre-commit hook nor any workflow; the wired set is sync-runtime-mirrors.cjs --check, codex sync-prompts.cjs --check, agent-roster-mirror-check and validate-command-tree-parity.sh.
Charter starting fact 1 ('46 authored markdown command files') is corrected to 35 authored commands plus 11 non-command markdown files.

The installed Devin binary has no command surface: devin --help lists no commands subcommand, and devin skills is documented as 'Manage agent skills (slash commands and agent-triggered context blobs)' — Devin's slash commands ARE skills.
Devin's only non-skill prompt-injection surfaces are --prompt-file <FILE> and the [PROMPT]... argument after --; neither registers a discoverable command entry point.
Devin's retired command mirror lived at .devin/skills/<cmd>/SKILL.md (35 entries at removal), not .devin/commands; a Devin command mirror is loadable only in skill shape.
Removal of the Devin command surface was an explicit operator directive with a BREAKING CHANGE note, reversing an earlier goal-hook packet; it is a decision, not drift.

The July decommission was partially reversed for the goal surface: .opencode/hooks/goal/devin/ and .devin/hooks/goal-inject.mjs exist again and are registered on SessionStart and UserPromptSubmit, while .devin/skills remains absent.

Devin's replacement affordance is native discovery of the 12 .opencode/skills/* packets as slash commands; none of the 35 authored .opencode/commands entry points (speckit, deep, create, doctor) has any Devin representation, so the /speckit:* lifecycle is unavailable in Devin.

Two Devin artifacts still describe the removed command surface: SYNC.md:74 uses '36 commands' as a present-tense teaching example, and the decommission commit explicitly deferred playbook scenarios DV-014..DV-016 for rewrite.

Three runtimes carry a skills mirror and each shape is runtime-constrained: .claude/skills and .pi/skills are whole-dir symlinks to ../.opencode/skills, while .hermes/skills holds 68 generated markdown-only copies because Hermes's static scanner quarantines symlinked directories (a whole-tree link cost ten minutes per session and quarantined every hub).

Hermes's 68 skill directories are 56 canonical SKILL.md copies plus 12 agent-<name> persona skills; the 56 reconciles exactly against a live count, because Hermes has no agent-file flag and a plugin prompt section is capped at 4000 characters.

Hermes has a live partial failure inside its generated mirror: only 61 of 68 skills load, because Hermes's own prose scanner quarantines 7 and excludes them from both 'skills list' and '-s'; the generator's --check cannot detect this, so green --check does not imply loadable skills.

Cursor's missing .cursor/skills is correct by nature (Cursor's skills live in ~/.cursor/skills-cursor/ and are Cursor-managed); the compensating affordance is the hand-authored .cursor/rules/skill-routing.md, whose packet list has no generator and will not pick up a new skill packet automatically.

Codex has no .codex/skills and no .codex/commands; its surface inventory enumerates seven surfaces with no skills row, and the equivalent affordance is 35 generated pointer-stub prompts plus a hand-authored AGENTS.md. Correct by nature, with the causal half inferred: the manifest asserts the absent directory without naming a missing loader capability.
Devin needs no skills mirror: it discovers .opencode/skills/* natively as slash commands, recorded in iteration 2 and re-confirmed at .devin/SYNC.md:20.
Documentation drift: .cursor/SYNC.md:32 claims commands/*.md (36); the live tree holds 35 (33 symlinks + goal-cursor.md + vision.md). The manifest a maintainer would trust overstates its own mirror.

sync-skills-hermes.cjs --check exists and is documented but is invoked by neither the pre-commit hook nor any workflow, joining sync-prompts-hermes.cjs --check and sync-prompts-pi.cjs --check as the third unwired drift mode.

Goal parity against the hub's own bar (injection and management bound to the same native identity): full = OpenCode and Pi; injection-only = Cursor and Devin; read-only projection = Hermes via the repo plugin; native-equivalent = Claude and Codex with no repo-side path.

The goal hub's per-runtime delivery table lists six runtimes and omits Hermes, which has a working binding (repo-guards-goal section, GOAL_RUNTIME=hermes, _goal_slice fallback); an auditor reading the hub would report a false gap or rebuild an existing path.
Cursor's and Devin's injection-only adapters are not read-only: both record a turn on the bound record, which is the one write they make.

Cursor's partial goal support is an identity limit, not an adapter limit: management needs a native session identity the prompt command does not carry, so /goal-cursor fails closed for every management action and answers only a session-free packet read. No adapter should be added.

Repo-side coverage for Claude/Codex exists and is wired (speckit YAML goal handover across plan/resume/implement/complete plus the always-on goal posture row at AGENTS.md:185 and CLAUDE.md:185), but the host goal command itself is only operator-confirmed and neither .claude/settings.json nor .codex/hooks.json carries a goal registration that would break if the host changed; Codex's coverage rests on a parity assumption derived from Claude's confirmation, and there is no goal-codex.md prompt stub.

Operator cost by runtime: Cursor/Devin do not re-read a mid-session bind (no refresh, no verify/continue); Claude/Codex fail silently if the host command is absent or renamed; Hermes's cost falls on maintainers through the missing doc row; OpenCode/Pi have none.

The agent roster is 12, not 13: .opencode/agents holds 12 md + README.txt, .codex/agents 12 toml, .pi/agents 12 md, .devin/agents 12 dirs. Each manifest's '(13)' counts the source tree's README.txt; the roster checker's own filter excludes it, and the off-by-one also reached a commit message ('PASS 13/13').

Two agent upstreams exist and two scripts each call a different one canonical: .opencode/agents is the authoring source for Codex/Pi generators and the Hermes symlink, while .claude/agents is what Cursor and Devin symlink into. check-agent-mirror-sync.cjs:5-9 and agent-roster-mirror-check.cjs:24 use the word 'canonical' for opposite trees.
Observed: check-agent-mirror-sync.cjs --all reports '12 agent(s) checked - all mirrors in sync - OK' with exit 0, so the OpenCode-Claude pairs are in sync under the gate's own contract today.

The agent mirror gate compares EXACT normalized token sets, not order or semantics; a live instance shows the blind spot: deep-research.md differs in body (37091 vs 37109 bytes) with one copy saying 'append idea_observed' and the other 'record idea_observed through the gateway', yet both token sets are 1188 tokens and identical after path normalization, so the gate passes. Token-set equality is not semantic equality.

Both executions of the mirror gate are change-scoped and skip when no agent file changed: pre-commit builds STAGED_AGENTS from git diff --cached for .opencode|.claude/agents only, and the PR workflow collects PR-range changed files only, exiting 0 when none changed.

Pi is the only uncovered generated agent tree: sync-agents-pi.cjs --check runs in neither the pre-commit MIRROR_CHECKS list nor the CI mirror-parity step, while Codex's equivalent is wired in both. Nothing would notice a Pi agent falling behind .opencode/agents.

Cursor, Devin and Hermes agent trees are symlinks (links into .claude/agents and .opencode/agents), so content drift is impossible and the only failure mode is a broken or replaced link, which agent-roster-mirror-check.cjs already resolves and catches.
Codex agent generation is a one-way lossy derivation: sandbox_mode, model and model_reasoning_effort cannot round-trip back to .opencode/agents.

Ten mirror generators exist (sync-runtime-mirrors, codex sync-prompts/sync-agents/generate-command-routers, hermes sync-prompts/sync-skills, pi sync-prompts/sync-agents, sync-hook-registrations, sync-gate1-pointers) plus check-agent-mirror-sync.cjs as a content gate; every generator implements --check.

The four hook registration files (.claude/settings.json, .codex/hooks.json, .cursor/hooks.json, .devin/hooks.v1.json) are GENERATED from hook-registry.json by sync-hook-registrations.cjs (render the hooks key, keep other keys), and --check runs at pre-commit and in CI.

Three manifest claims are false as written: .codex/SYNC.md:120 'hooks.json and config.toml are hand-authored. No generator produces them'; .devin/SYNC.md:31 'hooks.v1.json hand-authored'; .devin/SYNC.md:126 'hooks.v1.json is hand-authored and unmirrorable'. .devin/SYNC.md also contradicts itself at :46 ('re-run the generator'). A maintainer following :120 would hand-edit a generated file and be contradicted by the pre-commit gate.

Four working --check modes run in neither pre-commit nor CI: pi/sync-agents-pi.cjs, pi/sync-prompts-pi.cjs, hermes/sync-prompts-hermes.cjs, hermes/sync-skills-hermes.cjs — concentrated on the two translation-heavy runtimes. The pre-commit set is also one entry short of CI's (sync-gate1-pointers.cjs --check is CI-only).

Genuinely hand-maintained: .claude/mcp.json and settings.json non-hooks keys and statusline-command.sh; .codex/config.toml and AGENTS.md prose; .cursor/mcp.json and rules/skill-routing.md packet list; .pi/mcp.json, models.json, settings.json, statusline.sh and three pi-*config.json; .devin/config.local.json and mcp_config.json; .hermes holds only .gitkeep.

Drift instance (a): .cursor/SYNC.md:36 documents .cursor/mcp.json as a symlink with a double hop; it is a real file. Three independent copies exist (.claude, .cursor, .devin) and are currently byte-identical (md5 ae5cfafa...), while .pi/mcp.json differs by design (adds transport: stdio, lifecycle: lazy). Nothing would notice the first three diverging.

Drift instance (b): .cursor/rules/skill-routing.md names 8 of the 13 top-level skill packets; missing are mcp-code-mode, mcp-tooling, sk-communication, sk-vision and system-skill-advisor. This quantifies the known gap at .cursor/SYNC.md:114 and matters doubly because Devin reads the same rules file.

Cost ranks for the two worthwhile generators: extending sync-gate1-pointers.cjs to render the skill-routing packet list is low (machinery, canonical source, --check and two render targets all exist); a four-dialect MCP config generator is medium (claude/cursor/devin byte-identical today, pi needs a dialect map, pattern already proven by sync-hook-registrations.cjs). A .codex/config.toml generator is high cost and not recommended.

Hook architecture: 20 concern packages under .opencode/hooks/<concern>/<runtime>/, 29 hooks in hook-registry.json bound across four JSON runtimes (claude 21, codex 18, cursor 17, devin 21), with pi carrying a registry entry and no file at all.

Six concerns reach every runtime (completion, dispatch, mcp-route-guard, post-edit-quality, skill-advisor, spec-gate); three reach five of six (session-lifecycle lacks opencode, session-cleanup lacks pi, task-dispatch lacks codex).

Four hook absences are correct by nature and were already named by the Hermes parity work: codex-watchdog (OpenCode), directive-lifecycle (Claude), permission-policy (Devin, the only PermissionRequest host), hook-install; sk-vision absent for Claude is likewise documented ('Claude has no sk-vision integration').

Hook parity is the most complete surface in this research: after correcting two mechanism differences (Cursor reaches sk-vision through .cursor/rules/sk-vision.md rather than an adapter dir; Pi bundles dist-freshness, git-hooks-check, git-worktree-guard and git-primary-reconcile inside session-start-advisories.ts), the set of unported hooks is empty.

Pi's hook layer is the least protected surface: 'native code, not config' hand-authored extensions/*.ts, no hooks.json dialect, no registry bindings, and no drift checker — a shared-core behavior change surfaces only at runtime or in the manual-testing playbook. This compounds the two unwired Pi --check modes from iteration 6.

Hermes answers hook parity with a six-point bridge table in its plugin (pre_llm_call, pre_tool_call, transform_tool_result, pre_verify, on_session_start, four system-prompt sections, on_session_end) onto repo guard cores; every hook fails open, and the post-edit core deliberately runs in transform_tool_result because both hooks run on bounded worker threads and a post-hook stage would race the transform.

One flag vocabulary spans every runtime's hook adapter: hook-flags.env documents a master switch plus 22 per-concern switches read by shared hook-flags.{cjs,mjs,ts,sh}, with env overriding file. It is the only cross-runtime hook contract shared verbatim rather than translated.

.devin holds six entries in three ownership classes: real files (SYNC.md, mcp_config.json, config.local.json, generated hooks.v1.json), symlink trees (agents/ 12 dirs, hooks/ 21 links) and one whole-dir symlink (manual-testing-playbook).

Verified, not asserted: all 21 distinct .opencode/** scripts invoked by hooks.v1.json have a resolving symlink in .devin/hooks/ (0 missing, 0 broken) and all 12 .devin/agents/<name>/AGENT.md symlinks resolve (0 broken).

Devin can carry agents (nested AGENT.md symlinks), 8 hook events, MCP config (Devin-owned), skill-derived slash commands, one-shot prompts via --prompt-file/--, vision, 8 permission modes, playbook, subagents, plugins/cloud/ssh/acp. It cannot carry a mirrored command tree, a .devin/skills/ mirror (native discovery makes it unnecessary), a local .devin/rules/ directory (rules are inherited from Cursor/Claude/AGENTS.md), or goal management.

Devin is the only runtime with PermissionRequest and PostCompaction, but under the mode this repo dispatches with (--permission-mode bypass) PermissionRequest never fires so its adapter is inert, and PostCompaction has never been observed firing; PreToolUse still fires under bypass so guard coverage is intact.

Devin's strict frontmatter parser silently drops any file whose unquoted description contains a colon — historically hiding 12 of 36 commands with no warning — and no strict-YAML gate exists; it is the cheapest and most broadly protective detector available, because the files it checks are canonical for every runtime.

The cli-devin playbook's results table still shows unmarked PASS rows for superseded counts (DV-012 'all 13 roster agents', DV-014 '36/36 mirrored commands', DV-016 'all 36 command frontmatters'), mitigated only by a supersession note in the header; the same two numbers (13 agents, 36 commands) now appear in a third artifact.

A repo-authored surface can reach Devin in only four shapes: nested symlink, a generated entry in a Devin-owned registry (hooks.v1.json), a skill-shaped directory .devin/skills/<name>/SKILL.md (the shape the retired command mirror used, still supported because skills ARE the slash surface), or nothing at all (native discovery/inheritance/host-owned file). Shape 3 is the mechanism if the 35 commands should ever become Devin-reachable again.

There is no single parity gate: four automated entry points (pre-commit agent-mirror block + 6 checkers; spec-kit-check.yml with the same 6 plus sync-gate1-pointers; agent-mirror-sync.yml; command-tree-parity.yml) plus one manual read-only route (/doctor runtime-mirrors). Seventeen other workflows guard quality, not runtime parity.

The manual /doctor runtime-mirrors route covers strictly more than either automated gate: its upstream_assets include pi_agents and pi_prompts, which pre-commit and CI never run, and it carries a per-host hook-adapter fallback health table (file_exists per adapter behind every mkHookDrift chain) that detects degraded adapters rather than mirror shape.

Gate-by-gate blind spots: every existing checker asks 'is this mirror equal to its source?' and none asks 'does this runtime have a mirror for every surface that should reach it?' — so a whole surface can be absent while every gate passes, which is exactly the Devin command case. Additional named blind spots: token-set equality (agent bodies), change-scoped execution, Devin absent from command-tree parity, four --check modes invoked nowhere automatically, and no strict-YAML or Pi-extension checker.

Observed: command-catalog-mirror-check.cjs reports 'canonical: .opencode/commands frontmatter (35 commands)', 35/35 listed, STATUS=OK, exit 0 — independently confirming the iteration-1 correction to 35. Its own header comment still says 'the metadata covers 20 of the 39 shipped commands', so the checkers' prose drifts too.

Cheapest detector for the Devin command class: a surface-coverage assertion table (runtime x surface -> mirror | recorded exemption reason). The pattern already exists in agent-roster-mirror-check.cjs for the agents surface and in command-scope.cjs as the exemption registry for commands — but the latter is wired to generators, never used to assert coverage. Cost: one file walk, no new dependency, within the noise of the six checkers pre-commit already runs.

Second cheapest and broader: a strict-YAML frontmatter parse over every canonical agent and command file would catch the only silent failure class found in this research (Devin dropping files whose unquoted description contains a colon) and protects all seven runtimes at once.
The semantic agent-body divergence (deep-research.md) should not be automated: a similarity score would either fire constantly or miss it; the correct control is a review step.

openQuestions.statement: The 35 removed .devin/skills/<cmd>/ entries are stated as a count, not a roster; whether it maps one-to-one onto today's 35 authored commands is unconfirmed. Confirming check: list deleted paths in a2241041b0 and diff against the current command tree.

Whether the Codex CLI has any skill loader at all is inferred from an absence assertion in its SYNC manifest, not from the runtime's own contract. Confirming check: enumerate Codex's loader surfaces (config keys, --help, documentation).

Whether the Claude and Codex hosts actually expose a native goal command is unverified in-repo; the hub says operator-confirmed 2026-09-12 and re-checkable only against a live host. Confirming check: a live host probe.
